paragraphs: Moev sells mobile EV charging, sending a van with a charger to the vehicle instead of asking the driver to find a public charger. The site sets out three modes: scheduled top-ups at home, planned routes for fleets, and emergency roadside power for a driver who has run out. Pricing is set in an admin console and shown to the customer before the session rather than after it.

Fleet work is described as multi-EV depots and lots served on a recurring schedule, with mixed connectors handled in a single visit. Emergency roadside work is dispatched by phone and brings enough charge to reach the nearest fast-charger or the driver's home. A session is run by a Moev driver who connects the charger, reports kWh while it runs, and leaves an itemized receipt.
Coverage is given as Chicago Southland, with dispatch 7 days a week. Requests from outside that area are invited, and expansion is described as following where the calls come from.

quote.text: No public chargers, no waiting in line.
